newsitem.title: UK: UK's National Grid meets record electricity demand.
newsitem.headline: UK's National Grid meets record electricity demand.

text.p: The UK's National Grid Group Plc met peak demand of 49,730 megawatts, a new record, at 1700 GMT on Tuesday, the company said in a statement.
The company added that although temperatures were more severe last week, demand was lower as many businesses were still closed for the holiday.
The previous record of 48,811 megawatts was set on January 25, 1996, in a period of high winds and freezing conditions. Before that, the record demand was in January 1987 in heavy snow.
Electricity was supplied on Tuesday from 57 power stations to meet demand from 26 million customers, with additional supply coming from Scotland and France.
The National Grid has a notional capacity of 60,000 megawatts.
